step.detail:
Question: What are the stages of Your Service Your Say, any time limits to complain, and any response times or next steps? Quote exact lines.
Your Service Your Say has 4 stages: stage 1 is giving feedback directly to a staff member; stage 2 is a complaints officer handling the complaint; stage 3 is a review officer reviewing the stage 2 recommendations; and stage 4 is an external review by the Ombudsman or Ombudsman for Children. There is no overall time limit given for making a complaint on this page, but it says a manager will try to deal with it within 48 hours, a complaints officer will contact you within 5 working days if there needs to be an investigation, respond within 30 working days for a formal investigation, update you every 20 working days after that, and stage 3 is done within 20 working days unless more time is needed.

Question: What does this page say about how St James's Hospital was formed and whether it is a voluntary hospital or part of the public hospital system? Quote exact lines.
The page says St James’s Hospital was formed in 1971, and that it grew out of the closure of three small voluntary hospitals in Dublin. It does not say that St James’s Hospital itself is a voluntary hospital; instead, it says the new centre was funded and developed with the Department of Health and the HSE, which places it within the public health system context. The page says Ireland is developing Clinical Effectiveness through the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee (NCEC), which the Minister of Health set up in 2010, and that the NCEC recommends guidelines and audit to the Minister for Health for implementation in Irish healthcare. The page says the scheme covers State authorities, primarily the HSE and certain voluntary health and social care organisations with an indemnity from the Minister for Health. It says the scheme covers State authorities’ liability for their employees’ alleged clinical negligence, while the State authority remains the legal defendant and is responsible for damages and third-party costs.

Question: What does this page say about advertising phrases like no win no fee or free first consultation? Quote exact lines.
The page says these phrases are not permitted in certain ads about personal injuries: “no win no fee”, “no foal no fee” and “free first consultation”. It also says this prohibition applies only to advertisements that refer to personal injuries (or similar categories like motor accidents, workplace accidents, or public place accidents) as part of the legal services provided. Exact lines are below.
✓ quote found in the page: "Advertisements which use phrases “no win no fee”, “no foal no fee” and “free first consultation” or similar phrases which could suggest that legal services in connection with claims for personal injuries would be provided by the legal practitioner at no cost to the client."
✓ quote found in the page: "This prohibition only applies to advertisements which refer to personal injuries (or other words which describe categories of cases where claims for personal injuries may arise e.g. ‘motor accidents’, ‘workplace accidents’, ‘public place accidents’) as part of the legal services provided by the legal practitioner"

Question: What does this section say about the time limit for an action for damages for personal injuries, especially where the date of knowledge matters? Quote exact lines.
The section says an action for damages for personal injuries generally must be brought within three years from the cause of action accruing, or later from the injured person’s date of knowledge if that date is later. It also says that for certain actions under the 1980 Act, damages for personal injuries may be brought within two years of the date of knowledge if that is later than accrual.
✓ quote found in the page: "shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured."

sources.quote: Ireland is developing Clinical Effectiveness through the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee (NCEC) that the Minister of Health set up in 2010.

Clinical guidelines and clinical audit that successfully go through these steps are recommended to the Minister for Health through the Chief Medical Officer for endorsement and publications as NCEC National Clinical Guidelines or NCEC National Clinical Audit.

points: St James's says the Patient Experience Office manages feedback and complaints for the hospital.
St James's says it will acknowledge within 5 working days.
St James's says it will endeavour to provide a response within 30 working days.

steps.body: State Claims Agency / Clinical Indemnity Scheme
steps.what: For harm from care in an Irish public hospital, the official route found in this run is a clinical-negligence claim against the relevant State authority, with the State Claims Agency's Clinical Claims Unit taking over resolution under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme. I did not find an official no-fault or redress scheme for public-hospital medical harm in this run; the government page for the Personal Injuries Resolution Board describes its remit as motor, workplace, and public liability accidents instead.
steps.deadline: shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.
points: Under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, State authorities assume legal liability for employees' alleged clinical negligence.
When a claim is made, the State authority remains the legal defendant, and the State Claims Agency takes over responsibility for resolving the claim.
The Clinical Claims Unit manages claims taken against State authorities in connection with professional medical services.
The official limitation source found says an action for damages for personal injuries shall not be brought after three years from accrual or the injured person's later date of knowledge.
The government page for the Personal Injuries Resolution Board describes its remit as motor, workplace, or public liability accident claims, not clinical-negligence claims.
requires: A claim made against the relevant State authority / hospital under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme.
steps.appliesIf: Public hospital care where the hospital/HSE or another covered State authority is the defendant.
alternatives: Hospital complaint route for explanation/apology/service issues.
If the harm is from a motor, workplace, or public liability accident instead of clinical care, the Personal Injuries Resolution Board may apply.
missing: Exact defendant name for the treating service
Date of knowledge of the alleged negligence
Whether the patient wants damages for injury only or also financial losses

sources.quote: State authorities for the purposes of the Clinical Indemnity Scheme are primarily the HSE and organisations in the voluntary health and social care sector to which the Minister for Health has provided an indemnity in respect of clinical claims.
Under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, State authorities assume legal liability for their employees’ alleged clinical negligence.

When a claim is made against a State authority under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, the State authority remains the legal defendant and the State Claims Agency takes over responsibility for resolving the claim.

Under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, the State Claims Agency's Clinical Claims Unit manages clinical claims taken against State authorities in connection with the provision of professional medical services.
shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.

The Personal Injuries Resolution Board's role is to facilitate through mediation and/or assessment the settling of personal injuries compensation claims arising from motor, workplace, or public liability accident.
sources.publisher: Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment

steps.body: Legal Aid Board / Legal Services Regulatory Authority
steps.what: For an adult medical-negligence case in Ireland, the Legal Aid Board says it can provide legal advice and legal representation through its specialised Medical Negligence law centre, subject to financial eligibility and merits. In this run, the official fee-rule source found from the regulator was about advertising: phrases like 'no win no fee' are prohibited in certain personal-injury advertisements; I did not find an official cap on success fees in this run.
points: The Legal Aid Board says it can provide legal advice and legal representation in medical negligence.
The specialised unit is in Smithfield, Dublin, though local law centres can give more information.
To qualify for legal aid services you must have disposable income under €18,000.
The Board has an online financial eligibility indicator, but it only checks financial qualification and not the merits of the case.
The LSRA says ads using phrases such as 'no win no fee' and 'free first consultation' are prohibited in certain personal-injury advertisements.
steps.appliesIf: Adult civil legal aid / solicitor-funding questions in Ireland.
alternatives: Private funding with a solicitor, with costs information required under section 150 disclosures.
Local Law Centre contact if you do not want to use the online indicator.
missing: Approximate income, dependants, housing costs and savings for legal aid eligibility
Whether the patient wants legal aid or private representation

sources.quote: We can provide legal advice and legal representation in the area of Medical Negligence in our specialised Law Centre in Smithfield, Dublin.
However you can also contact your local Law Centre for more information.
To qualify for Legal Aid Services you must have disposable income under €18,000.
It will not tell you if you can actually get legal aid for your particular case, if you need representation in court, we will examine the merits of your case.

Advertisements which use phrases “no win no fee”, “no foal no fee” and “free first consultation” or similar phrases which could suggest that legal services in connection with claims for personal injuries would be provided by the legal practitioner at no cost to the client.

steps.body: Department of Health / National Clinical Effectiveness Committee (NCEC)
steps.what: In Ireland, the national body for the clinical guidance used across Irish healthcare is the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee under the Department of Health. It recommends guidelines to the Minister for Health to become NCEC National Clinical Guidelines for implementation in Irish healthcare.
points: The Minister for Health set up the NCEC in 2010.
The NCEC recommends guidelines and audit to the Minister for Health.
Guidelines that pass the process are published as NCEC National Clinical Guidelines.
steps.appliesIf: National clinical guidance used in Irish healthcare, including public hospitals.

sources.quote: Ireland is developing Clinical Effectiveness through the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee (NCEC) that the Minister of Health set up in 2010.

The role of the NCEC is to recommend guidelines and audit to the Minister for Health to become NCEC National Clinical Guidelines and NCEC National Clinical Audit for implementation in Irish healthcare.

Clinical guidelines and clinical audit that successfully go through these steps are recommended to the Minister for Health through the Chief Medical Officer for endorsement and publications as NCEC National Clinical Guidelines or NCEC National Clinical Audit.

sources.quote: The Patient Advocacy Service is independent, free and confidential.

steps.body: State Claims Agency / Clinical Indemnity Scheme
steps.what: For harm from care in an Irish public hospital, the official route found in this run is a clinical-negligence claim against the relevant State authority, with the State Claims Agency's Clinical Claims Unit taking over resolution under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme. I did not find an official no-fault or redress scheme for public-hospital medical harm in this run; the government page for the Personal Injuries Resolution Board describes its remit as motor, workplace, and public liability accidents instead.
steps.deadline: shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.
points: Under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, State authorities assume legal liability for employees' alleged clinical negligence.
When a claim is made, the State authority remains the legal defendant, and the State Claims Agency takes over responsibility for resolving the claim.
The Clinical Claims Unit manages claims taken against State authorities in connection with professional medical services.
The official limitation source found says an action for damages for personal injuries shall not be brought after three years from accrual or the injured person's later date of knowledge.
The government page for the Personal Injuries Resolution Board describes its remit as motor, workplace, or public liability accident claims, not clinical-negligence claims.
requires: A claim made against the relevant State authority / hospital under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme.
steps.appliesIf: Public hospital care where the hospital/HSE or another covered State authority is the defendant.
alternatives: Hospital complaint route for explanation/apology/service issues.
If the harm is from a motor, workplace, or public liability accident instead of clinical care, the Personal Injuries Resolution Board may apply.

sources.quote: State authorities for the purposes of the Clinical Indemnity Scheme are primarily the HSE and organisations in the voluntary health and social care sector to which the Minister for Health has provided an indemnity in respect of clinical claims.
Under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, State authorities assume legal liability for their employees’ alleged clinical negligence.

When a claim is made against a State authority under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, the State authority remains the legal defendant and the State Claims Agency takes over responsibility for resolving the claim.

Under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, the State Claims Agency's Clinical Claims Unit manages clinical claims taken against State authorities in connection with the provision of professional medical services.
shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.

The Personal Injuries Resolution Board's role is to facilitate through mediation and/or assessment the settling of personal injuries compensation claims arising from motor, workplace, or public liability accident.

steps.what: For an adult medical-negligence case in Ireland, the Legal Aid Board says it can provide legal advice and legal representation through its specialised Medical Negligence law centre, subject to financial eligibility and merits. steps.body: Department of Health / National Clinical Effectiveness Committee (NCEC)
steps.what: In Ireland, the national body for the clinical guidance used across Irish healthcare is the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee under the Department of Health. It recommends guidelines to the Minister for Health to become NCEC National Clinical Guidelines for implementation in Irish healthcare.
points: The Minister for Health set up the NCEC in 2010.
The NCEC recommends guidelines and audit to the Minister for Health.
Guidelines that pass the process are published as NCEC National Clinical Guidelines.
steps.appliesIf: National clinical guidance used in Irish healthcare, including public hospitals.

sources.quote: Ireland is developing Clinical Effectiveness through the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee (NCEC) that the Minister of Health set up in 2010.

The role of the NCEC is to recommend guidelines and audit to the Minister for Health to become NCEC National Clinical Guidelines and NCEC National Clinical Audit for implementation in Irish healthcare.

Clinical guidelines and clinical audit that successfully go through these steps are recommended to the Minister for Health through the Chief Medical Officer for endorsement and publications as NCEC National Clinical Guidelines or NCEC National Clinical Audit.

Data protection requests (https://www2.hse.ie/data-protection-and-your-rights/data-protection-requests/)
To request health records, the page says: "Complete the Subject Access Request form (PDF, 77 KB, 1 page)." says.detail:
Statute of Limitations (Amendment) Act, 1991, Section 3 (https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/1991/act/18/section/3/enacted/en/html)
The section says an action for damages for personal injuries generally must be brought within three years from the cause of action accruing, or later from the injured person’s date of knowledge if that date is later. It also says that for certain actions under the 1980 Act, damages for personal injuries may be brought within two years of the date of knowledge if that is later than accrual.
Quotes: "shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured." | "an action for damages under section 13 (7) of the said Act of 1980 which consist of or include damages in respect of personal injuries to any person may be brought within two years of the date of knowledge of the person injured if that date is later than the date on which the cause of action accrued."

says.text: Paying for help: Legal Aid Board / Legal Services Regulatory Authority. For an adult medical-negligence case in Ireland, the Legal Aid Board says it can provide legal advice and legal representation through its specialised Medical Negligence law centre, subject to financial eligibility and merits. In this run, the official fee-rule source found from the regulator was about advertising: phrases like 'no win no fee' are prohibited in certain personal-injury advertisements; I did not find an official cap on success fees in this run.

Compensation: State Claims Agency / Clinical Indemnity Scheme. For harm from care in an Irish public hospital, the official route found in this run is a clinical-negligence claim against the relevant State authority, with the State Claims Agency's Clinical Claims Unit taking over resolution under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme. I did not find an official no-fault or redress scheme for public-hospital medical harm in this run; the government page for the Personal Injuries Resolution Board describes its remit as motor, workplace, and public liability accidents instead.

For St James's public emergency care, the first step is the hospital/HSE complaint route through the Patient Experience Office under Your Service Your Say, with a 12-month complaint limit on St James's own leaflet. If that does not resolve things, the independent route is the Office of the Ombudsman after using the hospital/HSE complaints system; for compensation, the official route found is a clinical-negligence claim against the relevant State authority under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, with the State Claims Agency managing it.

trace.text: Read Stages in the Your Service Your Say process: Your Service Your Say has 4 stages: stage 1 is giving feedback directly to a staff member; stage 2 is a complaints officer handling the complaint; stage 3 is a…
trace.detail:
Question: What are the stages of Your Service Your Say, any time limits to complain, and any response times or next steps? Quote exact lines.
Your Service Your Say has 4 stages: stage 1 is giving feedback directly to a staff member; stage 2 is a complaints officer handling the complaint; stage 3 is a review officer reviewing the stage 2 recommendations; and stage 4 is an external review by the Ombudsman or Ombudsman for Children. There is no overall time limit given for making a complaint on this page, but it says a manager will try to deal with it within 48 hours, a complaints officer will contact you within 5 working days if there needs to be an investigation, respond within 30 working days for a formal investigation, update you every 20 working days after that, and stage 3 is done within 20 working days unless more time is needed.

Read Statute of Limitations (Amendment) Act, 1991, Section 3: The section says an action for damages for personal injuries generally must be brought within three years from the cause of action accruing, or later from the …
trace.detail:
Question: What does this section say about the time limit for an action for damages for personal injuries, especially where the date of knowledge matters? Quote exact lines.
The section says an action for damages for personal injuries generally must be brought within three years from the cause of action accruing, or later from the injured person’s date of knowledge if that date is later. It also says that for certain actions under the 1980 Act, damages for personal injuries may be brought within two years of the date of knowledge if that is later than accrual.
✓ quote found in the page: "shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured."
✓ quote found in the page: "an action for damages under section 13 (7) of the said Act of 1980 which consist of or include damages in respect of personal injuries to any person may be brought within two years of the date of knowledge of the person injured if that date is later than the date on which the cause of action accrued."
